claim: Down syndrome results in various degrees of cognitive deficits.
source: Down syndrome (DS) results in various degrees of cognitive deficits.
evidence: This is a general statement about DS presented in the abstract without specific data or citations in this sentence.

claim: In DS mouse models, recovery of behavioral and neurophysiological deficits using GABAAR antagonists led to hypothesize an excessive activity of inhibitory circuits in this condition.
source: In DS mouse models, recovery of behavioral and neurophysiological deficits using GABAAR antagonists led to hypothesize an excessive activity of inhibitory circuits in this condition.
evidence: This statement references prior work that used GABAAR antagonists to recover deficits, which led to a hypothesis about excessive inhibition.

claim: The dendritic synaptic inhibitory loop formed by somatostatin-positive Martinotti cells (MCs) and pyramidal neurons (PNs) was strongly enhanced in the prefrontal cortex of Ts65Dn mice.
source: In the prefrontal cortex of Ts65Dn mice (a well-established DS model), we found that the dendritic synaptic inhibitory loop formed by somatostatin-positive Martinotti cells (MCs) and pyramidal neurons (PNs) was strongly enhanced, with no alteration in their excitability.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There was no alteration in the excitability of Martinotti cells and pyramidal neurons in Ts65Dn mice.
source: In the prefrontal cortex of Ts65Dn mice (a well-established DS model), we found that the dendritic synaptic inhibitory loop formed by somatostatin-positive Martinotti cells (MCs) and pyramidal neurons (PNs) was strongly enhanced, with no alteration in their excitability.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on electrophysiological measurements.

claim: Perisomatic inhibition from parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons was unaltered in Ts65Dn mice.
source: Conversely, perisomatic inhibition from parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons was unaltered, but PV cells of DS mice lost their classical fast-spiking phenotype and exhibited increased excitability.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recording experiments.

claim: PV cells of DS mice lost their classical fast-spiking phenotype.
source: Conversely, perisomatic inhibition from parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons was unaltered, but PV cells of DS mice lost their classical fast-spiking phenotype and exhibited increased excitability.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on electrophysiological characterization of PV cells.

claim: PV cells of DS mice exhibited increased excitability.
source: Conversely, perisomatic inhibition from parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons was unaltered, but PV cells of DS mice lost their classical fast-spiking phenotype and exhibited increased excitability.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on electrophysiological measurements.

claim: Microcircuit alterations in Ts65Dn mice resulted in reduced pyramidal-neuron firing in vivo.
source: These microcircuit alterations resulted in reduced pyramidal-neuron firing and increased phase locking to cognitive-relevant network oscillations in vivo.
evidence: This is a finding from in vivo recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Microcircuit alterations in Ts65Dn mice resulted in increased phase locking to cognitive-relevant network oscillations in vivo.
source: These microcircuit alterations resulted in reduced pyramidal-neuron firing and increased phase locking to cognitive-relevant network oscillations in vivo.
evidence: This is a finding from in vivo recordings and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Down syndrome is a condition caused by full or partial trisomy of human chromosome 21.
source: Down syndrome (DS) is a condition caused by full or partial trisomy of human chromosome 21, characterized by various physical and neurological features including mild to severe intellectual disability (Antonarakis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DS, supported by a citation.

claim: Down syndrome is characterized by various physical and neurological features including mild to severe intellectual disability.
source: Down syndrome (DS) is a condition caused by full or partial trisomy of human chromosome 21, characterized by various physical and neurological features including mild to severe intellectual disability (Antonarakis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DS, supported by a citation.

claim: Individuals with DS present important deficits in cognitive tasks known to depend on the anatomical and functional integrity of the frontal lobe.
source: Individuals with DS present important deficits in cognitive tasks known to depend on the anatomical and functional integrity of the frontal lobe (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: DS is associated with an ultra-high risk for developing Alzheimer's disease.
source: Moreover, DS is also associated with other CNS-mediated phenotypes, including an ultra-high risk for developing Alzheimer's disease and high rates of autism for which the mechanisms are unknown (DiGuiseppi et al., 2010; Wiseman et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: DS is associated with high rates of autism.
source: Moreover, DS is also associated with other CNS-mediated phenotypes, including an ultra-high risk for developing Alzheimer's disease and high rates of autism for which the mechanisms are unknown (DiGuiseppi et al., 2010; Wiseman et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The mechanisms underlying the association of DS with Alzheimer's disease and autism are unknown.
source: Moreover, DS is also associated with other CNS-mediated phenotypes, including an ultra-high risk for developing Alzheimer's disease and high rates of autism for which the mechanisms are unknown (DiGuiseppi et al., 2010; Wiseman et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and represents a knowledge gap.

claim: Interventions to ameliorate DS-mediated cognitive dysfunctions are limited.
source: Interventions to ameliorate DS-mediated cognitive dysfunctions are limited.
evidence: This is a general statement about the current state of DS treatment.

claim: Mouse models of DS recapitulate several cognitive deficits of this condition.
source: Importantly, mouse models of DS recapitulate several cognitive deficits of this condition (Herault et al., 2017; Olmos-Serrano et al., 2016b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The Ts65Dn mouse line carries a partial trisomy of a segment of the mouse chromosome 16.
source: One of the best-characterized mouse models is the Ts65Dn mouse line (herein referred to as Ts), which carries a partial trisomy of a segment of the mouse chromosome 16 (Davisson et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation describing the mouse model.

claim: Ts mice recapitulate several dysfunctions present in DS individuals, such as reduced birthweight, male sterility, abnormal facial appearance and several cognitive impairments.
source: Ts mice recapitulate several dysfunctions present in DS individuals, such as reduced birthweight, male sterility, abnormal facial appearance and several cognitive impairments, including executive functions, such as working memory and cognitive flexibility (Olmos-Serrano et al., 2016b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Ts mice exhibit cognitive impairments including executive functions, such as working memory and cognitive flexibility.
source: Ts mice recapitulate several dysfunctions present in DS individuals, such as reduced birthweight, male sterility, abnormal facial appearance and several cognitive impairments, including executive functions, such as working memory and cognitive flexibility (Olmos-Serrano et al., 2016b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Recovery of behavioral and neurophysiological deficits underlying cognitive impairments using GABAA receptor blockers led to the hypothesis that intellectual deficits in DS are produced by an excessive activity of inhibitory circuits.
source: Recovery of behavioral and neurophysiological deficits underlying cognitive impairments using GABAA receptor blockers led to the hypothesis that intellectual deficits in DS are produced by an excessive activity of inhibitory circuits (Fernandez et al., 2007; Zorrilla de San Martin et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Direct evidence for over-inhibition in DS is lacking.
source: Nonetheless, direct evidence for over-inhibition in DS is lacking.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: The functional implications of the over-inhibition hypothesis at the network level, as well as the involvement of specific GABAergic circuits remain obscure.
source: Moreover, given the anatomical, molecular and functional diversity of cortical inhibitory neurons (Tremblay et al., 2016), the functional implications of this hypothesis at the network level, as well as the involvement of specific GABAergic circuits remain obscure.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap and is supported by a citation about interneuron diversity.

claim: Executive functions depend on the integrity of the prefrontal cortex.
source: Executive functions depend on the integrity of the prefrontal cortex (PFC), which plays an essential role in the synchronization of task-relevant, large-scale neuronal activity (Helfrich and Knight, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The prefrontal cortex plays an essential role in the synchronization of task-relevant, large-scale neuronal activity.
source: Executive functions depend on the integrity of the prefrontal cortex (PFC), which plays an essential role in the synchronization of task-relevant, large-scale neuronal activity (Helfrich and Knight, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Neuronal oscillations are rhythmic fluctuations of the electrical activity of single neurons, local neuronal populations and multiple neuronal assemblies, distributed across different brain regions.
source: An important network correlate of this synchronization is represented by neuronal oscillations: rhythmic fluctuations of the electrical activity of single neurons, local neuronal populations and multiple neuronal assemblies, distributed across different brain regions (Buzsáki and Wang, 2012).
evidence: This is a definition supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Oscillations are the result of a balanced and coordinated activity of excitatory pyramidal neurons and inhibitory neurons that use GABA as neurotransmitter.
source: Oscillations are the result of a balanced and coordinated activity of excitatory pyramidal neurons (PNs) and a rich diversity of inhibitory neurons that use γ-aminobutiric acid (GABA) as neurotransmitter.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the generation of oscillations.

claim: Parvalbumin (PV)-positive inhibitory interneurons form synapses onto the perisomatic region of PNs.
source: In particular, parvalbumin (PV)-positive inhibitory interneurons form synapses onto the perisomatic region of PNs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PV interneuron connectivity.

claim: PV cells tightly control PN spiking activity and drive network oscillations in the γ-frequency range (30–100 Hz).
source: PV cells thus tightly control PN spiking activity and drive network oscillations in the γ-frequency range (30–100 Hz) (Buzsáki and Wang, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: γ-Oscillations are necessary for several PFC cognitive functions, such as sustained attention and cognitive flexibility.
source: γ-Oscillations are necessary for several PFC cognitive functions, such as sustained attention (Kim et al., 2016b) and cognitive flexibility (Cho et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Martinotti cells (MCs) are somatostatin (SST)-positive interneurons that inhibit distal dendrites of PNs.
source: Conversely, Martinotti cells (MCs) are somatostatin (SST)-positive interneurons that inhibit distal dendrites of PNs, thereby controlling the integration of distal dendritic glutamatergic synaptic inputs originating from different regions of the brain (Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Martinotti cells control the integration of distal dendritic glutamatergic synaptic inputs originating from different regions of the brain.
source: Conversely, Martinotti cells (MCs) are somatostatin (SST)-positive interneurons that inhibit distal dendrites of PNs, thereby controlling the integration of distal dendritic glutamatergic synaptic inputs originating from different regions of the brain (Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Dendritic integration of multi-pathway inputs is necessary for working memory.
source: Dendritic integration of multi-pathway inputs is necessary for working memory (Abbas et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2016a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PV interneurons and MCs represent two major cortical inhibitory circuits, characterized by a precise division of labor during cortical activity.
source: Therefore, PV interneurons and MCs represent two major cortical inhibitory circuits, characterized by a precise division of labor during cortical activity.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on established knowledge about these interneuron types.

claim: Both PV interneurons and MCs were shown to be involved in the entrainment of network oscillations.
source: Both forms of inhibition were shown to be involved in the entrainment of network oscillations (Cardin et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2017; Sohal et al., 2009; Veit et al., 2017) and in the cognitive performance during medial (m)PFC-dependent tasks (Abbas et al., 2018; Cho et al., 2015; Cummings and Clem, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Both PV interneurons and MCs are involved in cognitive performance during medial (m)PFC-dependent tasks.
source: Both forms of inhibition were shown to be involved in the entrainment of network oscillations (Cardin et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2017; Sohal et al., 2009; Veit et al., 2017) and in the cognitive performance during medial (m)PFC-dependent tasks (Abbas et al., 2018; Cho et al., 2015; Cummings and Clem, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Inhibition from SST interneurons plays a crucial role in mPFC-dependent memory.
source: In particular, inhibition from SST interneurons plays a crucial role in mPFC-dependent memory (Abbas et al., 2018; Cummings and Clem, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Broad-spectrum GABAAR antagonists are not clinically viable, as they can yield undesired seizure-like activity and/or anxiety.
source: Broad-spectrum GABAAR antagonists are not clinically viable, as they can yield undesired seizure-like activity and/or anxiety.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the side effects of GABAAR antagonists.

claim: Treatment of Ts mice with selective and partial negative allosteric modulators of α5-containing GABAARs (α5 inverse agonist or α5IA) reverse cognitive behavioral and long-term synaptic plasticity deficits in DS mice.
source: Interestingly, however, treatment of Ts mice with selective and partial negative allosteric modulators of α5-containing GABAARs (α5 inverse agonist or α5IA) reverse cognitive behavioral and long-term synaptic plasticity deficits in DS mice (Braudeau et al., 2011; Duchon et al., 2020; Martínez-Cué et al., 2013; Schulz et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Neocortical dendritic synaptic inhibition of PNs from MCs relies on α5-containing GABAARs.
source: Importantly, neocortical dendritic synaptic inhibition of PNs from MCs relies on α5-containing GABAARs (Ali and Thomson, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The preference for α5-containing GABAARs was recently demonstrated at the equivalent hippocampal dendritic inhibitory circuit.
source: The preference for this specific GABAAR subunit was also recently demonstrated at the equivalent hippocampal dendritic inhibitory circuit (Schulz et al., 2019; Schulz et al., 2018), raising the question of whether dendritic inhibition is specifically altered in DS.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Dendritic inhibition from MCs onto PNs in Ts mice relied on α5-containing GABAARs in both Ts and control, euploid (Eu) mice.
source: We found that dendritic MC-PN synaptic inhibition relied on α5-containing GABAARs in both Ts and control, euploid (Eu) mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on pharmacological experiments.

claim: Bath application of α5IA (100 nM) produced a significant reduction of uIPSCs that was close to the maximal potency of the drug (~40%) in both Ts and Eu mice.
source: Indeed, in both genotypes, bath application of the selective negative allosteric modulator of α5-containing GABAARs, α5IA (100 nM; Sternfeld et al., 2004), produced a significant reduction of uIPSCs that was close to the maximal potency of the drug (~40%; Dawson et al., 2006; Figure 1b, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on pharmacological experiments, with reference to Figure 1b and Table 1.

claim: IPSC rise and decay times were not affected by α5IA application.
source: IPSC rise and decay times were not affected by α5IA application (data not shown).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on pharmacological experiments.

claim: MC-mediated uIPSC amplitudes were significantly larger in Ts compared to Eu mice.
source: Interestingly, MC-mediated uIPSC amplitudes were significantly larger and failure rate of synaptic responses evoked by the first action potential was significantly smaller in Ts compared to Eu mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1c and Table 1.

claim: Failure rate of synaptic responses evoked by the first action potential was significantly smaller in Ts compared to Eu mice.
source: Interestingly, MC-mediated uIPSC amplitudes were significantly larger and failure rate of synaptic responses evoked by the first action potential was significantly smaller in Ts compared to Eu mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1c and Table 1.

claim: The total amount of synaptic charge (Q) transferred during a train of 5 action potentials was near 5-fold larger in Ts than in Eu.
source: Moreover, the total amount of synaptic charge (Q) transferred during a train of 5 action potentials was near 5-fold larger in Ts than in Eu (Figure 1c, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1c and Table 1.

claim: MC-PN uIPSCs exhibited faster rise time in Ts as compared to Eu mice.
source: MC-PN uIPSCs exhibited faster rise time in Ts as compared to Eu mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Table 1.

claim: uIPSC decay time-constants were similar in Ts and Eu mice.
source: Yet, uIPSC decay time-constants were similar in the two genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Table 1.

claim: Glutamatergic recruitment of MCs by PNs was stronger in Ts than Eu mice.
source: We then examined glutamatergic recruitment of MCs by PNs and found that it was stronger in Ts than Eu mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings.

claim: Unitary excitatory postsynaptic currents (uEPSCs) in connected PN-MC pairs exhibited larger amplitude in Ts than Eu mice.
source: Unitary excitatory postsynaptic currents (uEPSCs) in connected PN-MC pairs exhibited larger amplitude, lower failure rate and larger charge transfer in Ts than Eu mice (Figure 1d, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1d and Table 2.

claim: Unitary excitatory postsynaptic currents (uEPSCs) in connected PN-MC pairs exhibited lower failure rate in Ts than Eu mice.
source: Unitary excitatory postsynaptic currents (uEPSCs) in connected PN-MC pairs exhibited larger amplitude, lower failure rate and larger charge transfer in Ts than Eu mice (Figure 1d, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1d and Table 2.

claim: Unitary excitatory postsynaptic currents (uEPSCs) in connected PN-MC pairs exhibited larger charge transfer in Ts than Eu mice.
source: Unitary excitatory postsynaptic currents (uEPSCs) in connected PN-MC pairs exhibited larger amplitude, lower failure rate and larger charge transfer in Ts than Eu mice (Figure 1d, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1d and Table 2.

claim: Short-term dynamics of MC-PN GABAergic synaptic transmission were depressing in both Ts and Eu mice.
source: Importantly, in both Ts and Eu mice, short-term dynamics of MC-PN GABAergic and PN-MC glutamatergic synaptic transmission were depressing and facilitating, respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings.

claim: Short-term dynamics of PN-MC glutamatergic synaptic transmission were facilitating in both Ts and Eu mice.
source: Importantly, in both Ts and Eu mice, short-term dynamics of MC-PN GABAergic and PN-MC glutamatergic synaptic transmission were depressing and facilitating, respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings.

claim: Short-term depression of MC-dependent dendritic inhibition onto PNs was more pronounced in Ts than Eu mice.
source: However, short-term depression of MC-dependent dendritic inhibition onto PNs was more pronounced in Ts than Eu mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Glutamatergic recruitment of MCs displayed the classical strong facilitating characteristics with no differences in short-term uEPSC dynamics in the two genotypes.
source: Conversely, glutamatergic recruitment of MCs displayed the classical strong facilitating characteristics (Silberberg and Markram, 2007) with no differences in short-term uEPSC dynamics in the two genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and a citation.

claim: Both MC-PN uIPSCs and PN-MC uEPSCs of Ts mice were characterized by a significant decrease of failure rate in all synaptic responses within the train.
source: Regardless of whether unitary synaptic responses exhibited significant alterations of short-term plasticity, both MC-PN uIPSCs and PN-MC uEPSCs of Ts mice were characterized by a significant decrease of failure rate in all synaptic responses within the train.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings.

claim: In Ts mice, GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses involved in the PN-MC-PN dendritic inhibitory loop increased their efficacy using different pre- and postsynaptic strategies.
source: These results on short-term plasticity suggest that, in Ts mice, GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses involved in the PN-MC-PN dendritic inhibitory loop increased their efficacy using different pre- and postsynaptic strategies.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the study.

claim: The dendritic inhibitory loop involving MCs and PNs is strengthened in Ts mice.
source: Overall, these results indicate that the dendritic inhibitory loop involving MCs and PNs is strengthened in Ts mice.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented in the study.

claim: Both output GABAergic synapses from MCs and their recruitment by local glutamatergic synapses were stronger and more reliable in Ts mice, as compared to their euploid littermates.
source: Both output GABAergic synapses from MCs and their recruitment by local glutamatergic synapses were stronger and more reliable in Ts mice, as compared to their euploid littermates.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented in the study.

claim: The firing frequency vs. injected current (f-i) curve was similar in both PNs and MCs in Eu and Ts mice.
source: The firing frequency vs. injected current (f-i) curve was similar in both cell types in Eu and Ts mice (Figure 2a,b; Tables 3–4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 2a,b and Tables 3–4.

claim: Single-action potential features and passive properties were similar in both genotypes except for a small but significant increase in action potential threshold of Ts PNs.
source: Furthermore, single-action potential features, and passive properties were similar in both genotypes except for a small but significant increase in action potential threshold of Ts PNs (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2; Tables 5–6).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2 and Tables 5–6.

claim: The density of GFP-expressing MCs was similar in both genotypes.
source: Importantly, the density of GFP-expressing MCs, and, in general, of SST-positive interneurons was similar in both genotypes (Figure 2c; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on immunohistochemistry, with reference to Figure 2c and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The density of SST-positive interneurons was similar in both genotypes.
source: Importantly, the density of GFP-expressing MCs, and, in general, of SST-positive interneurons was similar in both genotypes (Figure 2c; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on immunohistochemistry, with reference to Figure 2c and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The amplitude, failure rate and charge transfer of uIPSC trains evoked by action potentials in presynaptic PV interneurons were similar in both genotypes.
source: The amplitude, failure rate and charge transfer of uIPSC trains evoked by action potentials in presynaptic PV interneurons were similar in both genotypes (Figure 3a,b; Table 7).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 3a,b and Table 7.

claim: The amplitudes, failure rates and charge transfer of uEPSCs elicited by PN firing onto PV cells were indistinguishable in Eu and Ts mice.
source: Likewise, the amplitudes, failure rates and charge transfer of uEPSCs elicited by PN firing were indistinguishable in Eu and Ts mice (Figure 3c,d; Table 8).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 3c,d and Table 8.

claim: No difference was observed in short-term plasticity of both uIPSCs and uEPSCs in Ts and Eu mice at PV-PN synapses.
source: Consistently, no difference was observed in short-term plasticity of both uIPSCs and uEPSCs in Ts and Eu mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on paired recordings, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Intrinsic excitability of PV cells of Ts mice was strongly altered.
source: Surprisingly, however, we found that intrinsic excitability of PV cells of Ts mice was strongly altered.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings.

claim: PV cells in Ts mice required one fourth less current (rheobase) necessary to induce firing action potentials.
source: These interneurons required one fourth less current (rheobase) necessary to induce firing action potentials.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings.

claim: The gain of the f-I curves of Ts mice was dramatically reduced, as compared to their Eu littermates.
source: Accordingly, the gain of the f-I curves of Ts mice was dramatically reduced, as compared to their Eu littermates (Figure 4a–c; Table 9).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4a–c and Table 9.

claim: PV cells in Ts mice could not sustain high-frequency firing in response to 2 s-long depolarization.
source: Moreover, PV cells in Ts mice could not sustain high-frequency firing in response to 2 s-long depolarization, and the maximal spike rate was near half of that reached by PV cells in Eu mice (Figure 4a–c; Table 9).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4a–c and Table 9.

claim: The maximal spike rate of PV cells in Ts mice was near half of that reached by PV cells in Eu mice.
source: Moreover, PV cells in Ts mice could not sustain high-frequency firing in response to 2 s-long depolarization, and the maximal spike rate was near half of that reached by PV cells in Eu mice (Figure 4a–c; Table 9).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4a–c and Table 9.

claim: In Ts mice, action potential width of PV cells was 1.7-fold wider than that observed in Eu mice.
source: Notably, in Ts mice, action potential width was 1.7-fold wider and input resistance was 1.9-fold larger than that observed in Eu mice (Figure 4d,e,).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4d,e.

claim: In Ts mice, input resistance of PV cells was 1.9-fold larger than that observed in Eu mice.
source: Notably, in Ts mice, action potential width was 1.7-fold wider and input resistance was 1.9-fold larger than that observed in Eu mice (Figure 4d,e,).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4d,e.

claim: Action potential threshold and amplitude of PV cells were not affected in Ts mice.
source: Conversely, action potential threshold and amplitude were not affected (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Table 10).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Table 10.

claim: Abnormal passive and active properties of PV cells of Ts mice were present throughout all ages under study.
source: Abnormal passive and active properties of PV cells of Ts mice were present throughout all ages under study.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings across different ages.

claim: In Eu mice, PV-cell active and passive properties reached values similar to those reported for this cell type.
source: Importantly, in Eu mice, PV-cell active and passive properties reached values similar to those reported for this cell type (Kaiser et al., 2016; Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on current-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and a citation.

claim: The density of PV-INs in mPFC was similar in the two genotypes.
source: Similarly to SST cells, the density of PV-INs in mPFC was similar in the two genotypes (Figure 4f).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on immunohistochemistry, with reference to Figure 4f.

claim: Juxtacellular recordings from individual mPFC putative PNs revealed a near 50% decrease in the overall spiking rate in Ts mice as compared to their Eu littermates.
source: Juxtacellular recordings from individual mPFC putative PNs revealed a near 50% decrease in the overall spiking rate in Ts mice as compared to their Eu littermates (Figure 5b, Table 11).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 5b and Table 11.

claim: The difference in spiking rate was explained by a significant reduction of spiking rate during UP but not DOWN states.
source: This difference was explained by a significant reduction of spiking rate during UP but not DOWN states (data not shown).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings.

claim: Analysis of LFP power spectral density (PSD) did not show a significant difference in the two genotypes.
source: Analysis of LFP power spectral density (PSD) did not show a significant difference in the two genotypes (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 5c.

claim: In both genotypes, average stLFPs exhibited marked voltage deflections, indicating that spike probability was not randomly distributed but locked to LFP oscillations.
source: Interestingly, however, when we analyzed LFP waveform specifically during periods of neuronal spiking activity (spike-triggered LFP or stLFP), we found that, in both genotypes, average stLFPs exhibited marked voltage deflections, indicating that spike probability was not randomly distributed but locked to LFP oscillations (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 5d.

claim: The peak-to-peak amplitude of the stLFP was much larger in Ts than in Eu mice.
source: The peak-to-peak amplitude of the stLFP was much larger in Ts than in Eu mice (Figure 5d,e, Table 11), and, remarkably, the spectral power of the stLFP was largely increased in Ts mice, selectively in the β-γ-frequency band (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 5d,e, Table 11, and Figure 5f.

claim: The spectral power of the stLFP was largely increased in Ts mice, selectively in the β-γ-frequency band.
source: The peak-to-peak amplitude of the stLFP was much larger in Ts than in Eu mice (Figure 5d,e, Table 11), and, remarkably, the spectral power of the stLFP was largely increased in Ts mice, selectively in the β-γ-frequency band (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 5f.

claim: Ts mice exhibited significantly higher PPC values than Eu littermates for frequency bands ranging between 10 and 60 Hz.
source: Ts mice exhibited significantly higher PPC values than Eu littermates for frequency bands ranging between 10 and 60 Hz (Figure 4g, Table 12), thus revealing stronger phase locking selectively with β- and low γ-oscillations.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 4g and Table 12.

claim: Ts mice exhibited stronger phase locking selectively with β- and low γ-oscillations.
source: Ts mice exhibited significantly higher PPC values than Eu littermates for frequency bands ranging between 10 and 60 Hz (Figure 4g, Table 12), thus revealing stronger phase locking selectively with β- and low γ-oscillations.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on in vivo recordings, with reference to Figure 4g and Table 12.

claim: Enhanced dendritic inhibition by MCs in DS could underlie the deficits of long-term plasticity of glutamatergic synapses similar to those observed in the hippocampus of Ts mice.
source: Enhanced dendritic inhibition by MCs in DS could underlie the deficits of long-term plasticity of glutamatergic synapses similar to those observed in the hippocampus of Ts mice.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the findings of the study.
